content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text grounds an UNDERDETERMINED verdict on Matthew 1:16 not stating the begetter in either direction, which is the single-verse silence K-S2 governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.","room":"This is about one verse. It does not apply when the judge weighs two chains. — Reading 1: the verdict rests on Matthew 1:16's silence, so it is about one verse and K-S2 applies. Reading 2: the mention of Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4, and Numbers 1:2 means the judge is weighing two chains, so K-S2 does not apply.","why":"The judge treats the silence of Matthew 1:16 on the begetter as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED, exactly the single-verse ground K-S2 forbids."}
